source_text: Λευῗται, συνεργάται τρόπον τινὰ καὶ οἱονεὶ συλλήπτορες τοῖς ἱερουργοῖς ἐκνενέμηνται, φυλάξουσι γὰρ τὰς φυλακὰς αὐτοῦ, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τοῦ Ἀαρὼν, καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου, καὶ τὰ φυλάγματα τῶν υἱῶν. Ἰσραήλ. Καὶ μέχρι τούτων αὐτοῖς τῆς συνεργείας ὁ τρόπος. Ἐφίστησι δὲ τῇ σκηνῇ τόν τε Ἀαρὼν, καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ, καὶ «Φυλάξουσι» γὰρ, φησὶ, «τὴν ἱερατείαν ἑαυτῶν καὶ πάντα κατὰ τὸν βωμὸν, καὶ τὰ ἐσώτερα τοῦ καταπετάσματος,» τοῦτ' ἔστι τὰ ἀπόῤῥητά τε καὶ μυστικώτερα, καὶ ὅσα δρᾷν ἔθος τοὺς τῷ θείῳ προσεδρεύοντας θυσιαστηρίῳ· καὶ ἔστι μὲν ἀκραιφνῶς ὡς εἰς Χριστὸν ὁ τύπος, ὃν κατέστησεν ὁ Πατὴρ ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ, οὗ οἶκός ἐσμεν ἡμεῖς. Κατασημήνειαν δ' οὐκ ἀσυμφανῶς οἱ τῷ Ἀαρὼν συνιερατεύοντες, τῶν ἁγίων ἀποστόλων τὸν ἐναγῆ τε καὶ ἀξιάγαστον χορὸν, συνεργαζομένων ὥσπερ καὶ συλλειτουργούντων τῷ Χριστῷ. Θεοῦ γὰρ γεγόνασι συνεργοὶ, ταμίαι τε καὶ οἰκονόμοι μυστηρίων Θεοῦ, καὶ μὴν καὶ διάκονοι, δι' ὧν πεπιστεύκαμεν. Εἰ δέ τις ἕλοιτο καὶ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τὴν τάξιν πολυπραγμονεῖν, τὴν ἐν νόμῳ προανατύπωσιν, καταθαυμάσειεν ἂν εἰκότως. Ἐπισκόποις μὲν γὰρ, ἅτε δὴ τότε καθηγεῖσθαι λαχοῦσιν, καὶ μὴν τοῖς ἐπὶ τὴν μείω διέπουσι τάξιν, πρεσβυτέροις δέ φημι, πεπίστευται τὸ θυσιαστήριον, καὶ τὰ ἔσω τοῦ καταπετάσματος, οἷς ἂν πρέποι καὶ λέγεσθαι· «Καὶ φυλάξουσι τὴν ἱερατείαν αὐτῶν·» διακόνοις γε μὴν, τὸ, «Φυλάξουσι τὰς φυλακὰς τῆς σκηνῆς, καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη αὐτῆς, καὶ τὰ φυλάγματα τοῦ λαοῦ.» Ἢ οὐκ αὐτοὶ προστάττουσι διακεκραγότες ἐν ἐκκλησίαις, ποτὲ μὲν ὑμνολογεῖν ὅτι προσήκει λαοῖς, καὶ ἐν κόσμῳ μὲν ἑστάναι, κατηρεμεῖν δὲ πολλάκις, καὶ διανιστᾶσιν εἰς προσευχὰς, καὶ τῆς ἀναιμάκτου θυσίας ἐπιτελουμένης, αὐτοὶ προσκομίζουσι τὰ τῶν σκευῶν ἱερώτερα, καὶ λεπτὴν ἐφ' ἅπασι τοῖς ἀναγκαίοις ποιοῦνται τὴν ἐπιτήρησιν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἱερατεύουσι μὲν οἱ προὔχοντες, συλλαμβάνονται δὲ οἱ Λευῗται τῆς ἐκκλησιαστικῆς ἱερατείας τὴν τάξιν, τοῦ νομικοῦ προαναφωνοῦντος γράμματος. Ἐξείργεται δὲ τὸ δημοτικὸν παντὸς ἱεροῦ πράγματος, καὶ ὁ περὶ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἐπήρτηται λόγος τοῖς ἁρπάζουσι τὴν τιμήν. Τεθνήξεται γὰρ, φησὶν, ἢν αὐτόμολός τις ἐπ' αὐτὴν ἔλθῃ, τὴν θείαν ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ ψῆφον οὐκ ἔχων. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἀσύντακτον μὲν ταῖς τῶν ἄλλων ἀπογραφαῖς τὸ Λευϊτικόν, πλὴν ἀνάγραπτον ἰδικῶς καὶ ἐν βίβλῳ Θεοῦ· «Καὶ ἐλάλησεν» γὰρ, φησὶ, «Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ Σινᾶ λέγων· Ἐπίσκεψαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Λευῒ κατ' οἴκους πατριῶν αὐτῶν, κατὰ δήμους αὐτῶν, κατὰ συγγενείας αὐτῶν. Πᾶν ἀρσενικὸν ἀπὸ μηνιαίου καὶ ἐπάνω, ἐπίσκεψαι αὐτούς· καὶ ἐπεσκέψαντο αὐτοὺς Μωσῆς καὶ Ἀαρὼν διὰ φωνῆς Κυρίου, ὃν τρόπον συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς Κύριος. Καὶ ἦσαν οὗτοι οἱ υἱοὶ Λευῒ ἐξ ὀνομάτων αὐτῶν, Γεδσὼν, Καὰθ, καὶ Μεραρί· ταῦτα τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν
pass_a_gloss: [Cyril, continuing] [So the] Levites have been allotted in some way as co workers and as it were helpers to the sacred rite performers; for they will keep his charges, clearly Aaron's, and all the vessels of the tent of witness, and the guard duties of the sons of Israel; and up to these things is the manner of their co working. He sets over the tent Aaron and his sons with him; for they will keep, he says, their own priesthood and all at the altar and the things further inside the veil, that is, the unspeakable and more mystical things, and whatever those attending the divine altar are accustomed to do. And the type is purely toward Christ, whom the Father appointed over his house, whose house we are. Those co serving as priests with Aaron would signify not unclearly the holy and admirable chorus of the holy apostles, as co working and co ministering with Christ. For they became God's co workers, treasurers and stewards of God's mysteries, and indeed ministers through whom we have believed. If one would choose to examine also the order of the Church, the prefiguration in the law, he would fittingly marvel. For to bishops, as having obtained by lot to lead, and to those administering the lesser rank, I mean presbyters, has been entrusted the altar and the things inside the veil; to them it would fit to be said: and they will keep their priesthood; but to deacons: they will keep the charges of the tent and all its vessels and the guard duties of the people. Or do they not themselves command, crying out in churches, sometimes that it befits the peoples to sing hymns, and to stand in order, and often to be quiet, and rouse to prayers, and when the bloodless sacrifice is being accomplished, they themselves bring the more sacred of the vessels, and make fine/careful watch over all necessary things? [Palladius] Very much. [Cyril] So the preeminent act as priests, and the Levites take part in the order of the ecclesiastical priesthood, the legal letter proclaiming beforehand. The commoners are excluded from every sacred matter, and the word about the last things (i.e. the extreme penalty) hangs over those who snatch the honour. For he will die, it says, if anyone self moved comes to it, not having the divine vote upon himself. [Palladius] True. [Cyril] So the Levitical [tribe] is unranked with the enrollments of the others, but registered specially also in God's book; for the Lord spoke, it says, to Moses in the desert of Sinai: quote of LXX Numbers 3:14–17: number/visit the sons of Levi by houses of their fathers, by peoples/clans, by kinships; every male from a month old and up, number them; Moses and Aaron numbered them through the voice of the Lord as the Lord ordered; these were the sons of Levi by names: Gershon, Kohath, Merari; these the names of the [continues in section 4].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …Levites have been assigned as fellow workers, in a way, and helpers, as it were, to those who perform the sacred rites. For ‘they shall keep his charges’ (meaning, clearly, Aaron’s) ‘and all the furnishings of the tent of witness, and the charges of the sons of Israel’ (Numbers 3:7–8). Their share in the work goes this far. But he sets over the tent both Aaron and his sons with him; for ‘they shall keep,’ he says, ‘their own priesthood and all that concerns the altar, and the things within the veil’ (Numbers 3:10), that is, the secret and more mystical things, and all that those who wait on the divine altar are accustomed to do. And the type, in its pure sense, points to Christ, whom the Father appointed over his house, whose house we are (Hebrews 3:6). And those who share the priesthood with Aaron would signify, clearly enough, the sacred and admirable company of the holy apostles, who work and minister, as it were, together with Christ. For they have become God’s fellow workers (1 Corinthians 3:9), treasurers and stewards of the mysteries of God (1 Corinthians 4:1), and also ministers through whom we have believed (1 Corinthians 3:5). And if anyone should choose to look closely at the order of the Church as well, he would rightly marvel at the way the law sketched it in advance. For to the bishops, since it has fallen to them to preside, and also to those who hold the lesser rank (I mean the presbyters), the altar and the things within the veil have been entrusted; and these words would fit them: ‘And they shall keep their priesthood’ (Numbers 3:10). To the deacons belongs: ‘They shall keep the charges of the tent, and all its furnishings, and the charges of the people’ (Numbers 3:7–8). Or is it not they who call out in the churches and direct the people, now to sing hymns as is fitting, now to stand in good order, often to keep silence? Do they not rouse them to prayer, and, when the bloodless sacrifice is being offered, themselves bring forward the more sacred vessels and keep careful watch over everything needed?

Cyril: So those of the first rank serve as priests, while the Levites help in the order of the Church’s priesthood, as the letter of the law proclaimed in advance. The common people are shut out from every sacred task, and the sentence of the extreme penalty hangs over those who seize the honor. For if anyone comes to it of his own accord, it says, without having God’s vote in his favor, he shall die (Numbers 3:10).

Cyril: So the Levitical tribe is not counted in with the enrollments of the others; yet it is registered separately, and in God’s book too. For ‘the Lord spoke,’ it says, ‘to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying: Number the sons of Levi by their fathers’ houses, by their clans, by their families; every male from a month old and upward, number them. And Moses and Aaron numbered them at the word of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded them. And these were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon, Kohath and Merari. These are the names of the… (Numbers 3:14–18)

apparatus.note: Numbers 3:7–8 and 3:10 are re-quoted in adapted form (for the deacons Cyril writes 'the charges of the people' for 'the sons of Israel'); cited to the verses they adapt. The death clause in the third Cyril turn ('he shall die ... if anyone comes to it on his own initiative') paraphrases Numbers 3:10. Possible uncited allusion: Hebrews 5:4 (no one takes the honour for himself unless called by God) behind 'those who seize the honour' and 'God's vote'. ἐναγής normally means 'accursed', but patristic usage (Lampe) has 'holy, pure'; context demands 'holy'. ἅτε δὴ τότε καθηγεῖσθαι λαχοῦσιν: τότε is awkward (perhaps a misprint for τό); rendered by sense 'since it has fallen to them to preside'. The bishops-and-presbyters clause: Cyril assigns the altar and 'within the veil' to both bishops and presbyters (the presbyters being 'the lesser rank'); kept as written. 'Bloodless sacrifice' (ἀναίμακτος θυσία) is the eucharistic offering; kept as a liturgical term. Numbers 3:16 in the LXX names 'Moses and Aaron' as numbering; Hebrew-based English has Moses alone; translated as Cyril gives it. Section ends mid-quotation; the names of Gershon's sons open section 4. Reviewer: the quotation is cited 3:14–18 because its last words ('These are the names of the') open LXX Numbers 3:18, which continues in section 4 (3:18–20).
